row.team_price_text: Base: starting at $7 per report, unlimited users
row.evidence: SAP Concur's developer docs describe a SCIM 2.0-based User Provisioning Service and Identity v4.1 API for Expense, Travel, Invoice and Request (Standard and Professional editions), but the pricing page (Base $7/report, Plus $11/report, Premium custom) does not say which plan includes provisioning.
row.notes: Per-report pricing: Base from $7 per report and Plus from $11 per report (both unlimited users, 'Buy now'), Premium custom. Neither the pricing page nor the plan comparison mentions SSO, SCIM or APIs, so the SCIM plan is unknown. Provisioning is through SAP Concur's SCIM 2.0-shaped Identity v4.1 and User Provisioning Service (UPS) v4 APIs (Users, Bulk, ServiceProviderConfig, Schemas, ResourceTypes, PATCH/PUT, filter), authenticated with company-level OAuth tokens; generating your own Client ID needs the OAuth 2.0 Application Management tool, which must be enabled by SAP Concur Client Web Services. UPS also writes Spend and Travel extensions and roles. Hard DELETE is not recommended and only for users with no transaction history. The Okta OIN app marks SCIM Create/Update/Deactivate; Microsoft Entra provisions via SAP Cloud Identity Services rather than directly.

scim.notes: Not a toggle-and-token SCIM endpoint: it is SAP Concur's SCIM 2.0-shaped platform API, called with company-level OAuth access tokens. UPS needs Concur Expense and/or Concur Travel.

auth.token_source: Administration > Company > Authentication Admin > Company Request Token (with an App ID / Client ID); Client IDs come from the OAuth 2.0 Application Management tool once Client Web Services enables it

endpoints.notes: No Groups resource is documented in Identity v4.1 or UPS v4; roles are written through the Spend extension.

deprovision.data_retained: Users with transaction history fall under the Data Retention policy; hard DELETE is only for users with no transaction history.

attributes: any User schema attribute (booleans, strings, numbers, dates, lists) via POST /Users/.search

custom.how: SAP Concur Spend (urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:spend:2.0:User) and Travel (urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:travel:2.0:User) extensions through UPS.

roles.how: UPS provisions a user's roles (Spend role codes) along with the profile.

limitations.text: Access to this documentation does not provide access to the API.
UPS requires the customer to have purchased Concur Expense or Concur Travel.
UPS is asynchronous: each request returns a provisionId to poll; /Bulk/ takes up to 100 operations.

user_api.notes: The user-management API is the same SCIM-shaped Identity v4.1 / UPS v4 surface. Plan and price of Client Web Services access are not published.

endpoints.purpose: UPS: provision a user (identity, spend, travel)

okta.notes: OIN page marks SAML, SWA, SCIM, Entitlement Management and Create/Update/Deactivate/Schema Discovery as checked (read from page markup); Group Push not checked.

entra.notes: Entra gallery app 'Concur' does SAML SSO with just-in-time user creation; Entra provisioning goes to SAP Cloud Identity Services, whose Identity Provisioning then provisions SAP Concur.

fallbacks.other_sync: SAP Cloud Identity Services Identity Provisioning (SAP IPS) as an intermediary from Entra and other sources; HR feeds through the UPS /Bulk/ endpoint.
fallbacks.notes: Microsoft's Entra tutorial says Concur supports just-in-time user provisioning on SSO; no SAP Concur page confirming this was loaded.
